answer.text:
**Enrollment Deadlines**

- **Tuition-Free Full-Time Program (Texas Residents Only):**
  - Enrollment is limited and uses a lottery system.
  - **Spring/Mid-Year Lottery:** Held October 29, 2026, for students transferring mid-year.
  - **First Semester:** Course enrollments open August 3, 2026; courses must be completed by January 15, 2027.
  - **Second Semester:** For current students, enrollments open December 16, 2026; for new students, enrollments open January 4, 2027; courses must be completed by June 30, 2027.
  - Enrollment continues until the pre-established cap is reached. In between lotteries, enrollment may open if space becomes available.
  - **Automatic Re-Enrollment:** Current students must submit a re-enrollment form for the next school year; no reapplication is necessary.

- **Tuition-Paid Programs (Outside TX or TX Residents Seeking More Flexibility):**
  - Enrollments can occur at any time as long as space is available.

**Required Documents**

- **For Tuition-Free Full-Time Program:**
  - **Birth Certificate**
  - **Proof of Texas Residency** (must include the student’s or parent/guardian’s name and a Texas residential address). Acceptable documents include:
    - Current deed
    - Current lease or mortgage statement
    - Current utility bill (gas, water, internet, or electric; disconnect notices not accepted)
    - Current documents from the U.S. military or Veterans Administration indicating residential address
    - Letter of Texas residency issued by the Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD)
  - **Unofficial Transcript**
    - For homeschool students: Provide a transcript and be prepared to take Credit By Exams (CBEs) for grade placement.

- **For Tuition-Paid Full-Time Program:**
  - **Birth Certificate**
  - **Previous Transcripts** (if applicable)

**Additional Notes**

- All applicants must have access to a computer that meets minimum technology requirements and reliable internet access.
- A designated Learning Coach (parent/guardian or another responsible adult) is required for the tuition-free program.
- State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR)/End of Course (EOC) exams are required for tuition-free students.

**Next Steps**

- To apply, complete the intake form: [Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form](https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/apply/?_gl=1*v05loa*_gcl_au*NTY5NzA2ODU2LjE3MzA4NDA5OTY.*_ga*MjU0NDE2Nzg2LjE3MjMwNDQ2MTA.*_ga_TSPQSJQPQF*MTczMzI2MjA5Ni4xNzkuMS4xNzMzMjYyMTA1LjAuMC4w)
- For questions or support, contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

query.raw: Can she enroll for just one semester and transfer back to her current high school?

chunks.text:
Grade-Level Placement

Students transferring from an accredited public or private school will be placed in the appropriate grade level and semester courses based on the most recently completed semester as indicated on the student’s report card or other academic records from the previous school.

Texas Tech K-12 courses are designed for students to begin at the start of a semester whenever possible. Students are encouraged to complete the current semester at their previous school before withdrawing and enrolling with Texas Tech K-12.

Students who transfer before completing a semester may be assigned intervention coursework, required to repeat the previous semester or asked to complete placement assessments to assist with appropriate grade-level and course placement.

Grade Level Placement for Transfer Students

Students transferring to Texas Tech Middle School from an accredited public or private school will generally be placed at the grade level indicated by their previous school. An official transcript, report card or other required academic record must be provided to verify previous enrollment, completed coursework and grade-level placement.

Texas Tech K-12 courses are designed for students to begin at the start of a semester whenever possible. Students are encouraged to complete their current semester before withdrawing from their previous school.

Students who transfer before completing a semester may be required to complete additional coursework, intervention or placement assessments to determine appropriate course and grade-level placement.

Students transferring from a homeschool program or non-accredited school or program must provide available academic documentation, such as transcripts, grade reports or records of completed coursework. Texas Tech K-12 will review the student’s academic history and may require placement assessments or other academic evaluation to determine appropriate grade-level and course placement.

Texas Tech K-12 reserves the right to make the final determination regarding grade-level and course placement.

How is taking a single course different from the Full-Time Diploma Program?

To take a single course, students do not need to withdraw from their current school. Students need to obtain approval from their current school Counselor or Principal before enrolling. Students should coordinate with their school Counselor concerning their local school policies and other requirements.

Concurrent Diploma

Two Schools. Two Diplomas. More Opportunity.

The Concurrent Diploma pathway allows eligible students to work toward two high school diplomas simultaneously:

A diploma from their local school + a Texas high school diploma from Texas Tech K-12.

Students complete a combination of Texas Tech K-12 online courses and eligible coursework transferred from their local school.

This pathway may be a good fit for students who:

Step 1: Want to remain enrolled in their local school

Step 2: Want the opportunity to earn a U.S. high school diploma

Step 3: Are prepared to complete coursework in English

Step 4: Want to expand their academic experience while completing their local education

Students must demonstrate adequate English language skills to succeed in the program. Entrance exams are used to help assess academic and English proficiency before admission.

Concurrent Diploma

Two Schools. Two Diplomas. More Opportunity.

The Concurrent Diploma pathway allows eligible students to work toward two high school diplomas simultaneously:

A diploma from their local school + a Texas high school diploma from Texas Tech K-12.

Students complete a combination of Texas Tech K-12 online courses and eligible coursework transferred from their local school.

This pathway may be a good fit for students who:

Step 1: Want to remain enrolled in their local school

Step 2: Want the opportunity to earn a U.S. high school diploma

Step 3: Are prepared to complete coursework in English

Step 4: Want to expand their academic experience while completing their local education

Students must demonstrate adequate English language skills to succeed in the program. Entrance exams are used to help assess academic and English proficiency before admission.

Who Can Apply

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 graduates currently enrolled at Texas Tech University or transferring

Step 2: Graduates of the Texas Tech K-12 high school diploma program

Full-Time Options for Students

For students who may need an alternative to a traditional school environment, districts may also recommend the Texas Tech K-12 online high school diploma program.

Students who enroll full-time transfer to Texas Tech K-12 to complete their coursework through our flexible online program.

Texas Tech K-12 Middle School - Full-Time

The Texas Tech K-12 middle school program is an engaging and rigorous program that prepares students by forming the foundation for high school. Students enrolled full-time in middle school will complete all core courses in addition to one year of Fine Arts and one year of Career Exploration.

Required core courses include:

Step 1: Career Exploration

Step 2: Fine Arts

Step 3: Language/Reading Arts

Step 4: Math

Step 5: Science

Step 6: Social Studies

Academically strong students have the opportunity to get ahead through credit by exams and enrolling in approved high school courses.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification Of Enrollment and Student ID (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in PSAT, ACT, AND SAT exams.

Link for "Student ID (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/resources/documents/IdentityVerification.pdf

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

Link for "Supplemental Program (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/courses/

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

Weighted Coursework

Eligible Advanced Placement (AP), Honors, International Baccalaureate (IB) and Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit courses receive additional GPA weight in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 policy.

Eligible transferred coursework with an approved weighted-course designation may also receive the corresponding GPA weight when applied toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

Transfer Grades for the High School Program

Students transferring to Texas Tech High School from an accredited public or private school must provide an official transcript, report card or other required academic records for evaluation.

Texas Tech K-12 will review eligible coursework to determine which credits may be applied toward the student’s Texas Tech High School graduation requirements. Transfer grades from accredited schools are included in the student’s GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.

Students transferring from a homeschool program or non-accredited school or program must provide appropriate academic documentation, such as transcripts or grade reports, for review. Grades from homeschool or non-accredited programs are not directly transferable for credit. Students may earn applicable credit by completing the appropriate CBE or by enrolling in the corresponding course.

Texas Tech K-12 reserves the right to make the final determination regarding the acceptance and application of transferred coursework toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

The following designations will receive weighted credits:

Step 1: Advanced Placement (AP) or Passing (P)

Step 2: Honors

Step 3: International Baccalaureate (IB)

Step 4: Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit

All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses taken by a student that apply to graduation will be used to compute the Grade Point Average, excluding any approved Physical Education Substitution (SUBPRO) credits and local credit courses.

Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will make every effort to assist students in transferring grades and credits from accredited public or private schools as allowed by Texas Education Agency (TEA) policies and Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). An official transcript or report card will be required for credit transfer.

Public or Private School Transfer Grades Conversion to Texas Tech K-12 | Public or Private School Transfer Grades Conversion to Texas Tech K-12

Can students with Individualized Education Program (IEPs) or 504 plans enroll?

Step 1: Yes, if the online program is appropriate for their needs. The ARD or 504 committee must agree it’s the right fit for your child.

answer.text:
**Enrolling in Texas Tech K-12 for One Semester and Transferring Back**

- Texas Tech K-12 allows students to enroll in individual courses or for a single semester as a supplemental/part-time student. You do not need to withdraw from your current school to take a single course or semester with Texas Tech K-12.
- If the student wishes to enroll full-time for just one semester and then transfer back to her current high school, this is possible, but there are important considerations:
  - **Approval Required:** Before enrolling, you must obtain approval from your current school counselor or principal to ensure that credits earned at Texas Tech K-12 will be accepted and applied toward graduation or grade advancement at your current high school.
  - **Credit Transfer:** Each school or district sets its own policies for accepting transfer credits. Confirm with your current school that they will accept the Texas Tech K-12 credits before enrolling.
  - **Course Completion:** Students have up to six months to complete each course. Plan your enrollment and course completion to align with your intended return to your current high school.

**Next Steps**
- Speak with your current school counselor to discuss your plan and get written approval for the courses or semester you wish to take at Texas Tech K-12.
- Enroll in the desired courses or as a full-time student for one semester through the Texas Tech K-12 application process.

    - Plan for **5–6 hours per week per course**.

You may request a Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) VOE Form or an official letter verifying enrollment and attendance from your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. Request a VOE by emailing a request to your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. The advisor will require at least two working days for progress review.
